name: Auto-assign the correct price book or price list to a deal by rule
body:
- **name:** Auto-assign the correct price book or price list to a deal by rule
- **user_flow:**
  1. HubSpot: `CRM > Products` → **Manage price books** → open a price book → hover **Assignment rules** → click the **edit icon**.
  2. HubSpot: in **Filters** click **+ Add filter** → configure deal-property filters (`and` / `or` groups) → review the matching deals in the right panel → toggle **Auto-assigned** on → **Save** → toggle the price book's **Inactive** switch off to activate.
  3. HubSpot: three modes are chosen deliberately — *No assignment rules* (manual only), *Assignment rules without auto-assignment* (test first), *Assignment rules with auto-assignment*.
  4. HubSpot override: on the deal's *Line items* card click **Price book: None** (or the price book name) → **Price book** dropdown → **Change price book**. Changing the price book removes previously added line items.
  5. Dynamics 365 Sales: enable the Sales tab system setting (or set `Organization.UseInbuiltRuleForDefaultPriceSelectionRule = 1`), associate a price level with a **Territory** using the **Territory Default Pricelist** connection role, and assign the territory to the user. Single match → price level set automatically; multiple matches → the user must choose.
- **data_flow:** Deal/company property values (HubSpot) or the acting user's sales territory (Dynamics) → filter/condition evaluation → one matching price book / price level is written onto the deal/quote header (`pricelevelid` in Dynamics) at creation → the product lookup and line-item price resolution are then scoped to that book, so only that book's products/prices/terms are browsable when adding line items → the quote inherits the price book from the deal.
- **data_sources:** HubSpot deal properties, company properties, price book object. Dynamics `territory`, `pricelevel`, `systemuser`, `organization.UseInbuiltRuleForDefaultPriceSelectionRule`.
- **apis_hit:** HubSpot — properties API (`GET /crm/properties/...`), deal object `PATCH` for the price book association. Dynamics — **`GetDefaultPriceLevelRequest`** message ("Dynamics 365 internally uses the `GetDefaultPriceLevelRequest` message to determine the default price level"), registrable as a plug-in: "Register the plug-in on the `GetDefaultPriceLevel` message."
- **automations:** Auto-assignment runs when a deal row is created ("Price books are auto-assigned only when a deal is created. After a price book is auto-assigned, HubSpot won't run auto-assignment again if the deal or associated company properties used in the filter are updated"). Dynamics `GetDefaultPriceLevel` fires on create/update of opportunity/quote/order/invoice rows.
- **features_tools:** HubSpot price book assignment-rule editor, deal *Line items* card price-book selector, Super Admin override. Dynamics System Settings → Sales tab, territory form + **Territory Default Pricelist** connection role, plug-in registration on `GetDefaultPriceLevel`.
- **extensibility:** HubSpot — "if multiple price books match, the deal owner can choose which matching price book to use"; Super Admins can override; turning **off** the *Create custom line items* permission forces price-book-only behaviour. Dynamics — replace the built-in rule with a plug-in that returns your own price level.
- **sources:**
  - https://knowledge.hubspot.com/products/use-price-books
  - https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/sales/developer/set-default-price-level-for-opportunity-quote-order-invoice
  - https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/sales/create-edit-quote-sales
- **evidence:** "When a deal matches exactly one assignment rule, that price book is automatically assigned." · "If multiple price books match, the deal owner can choose which matching price book to use." · "Quotes inherit the price book from the associated deal. Users can't select a price book when creating a quote; they must select it on the deal." · "If the price book is changed, any line items associated with the previous price book will be removed." · Dynamics: "If a single price level is returned, the price level is automatically set … If multiple price levels are returned, the price level field isn't populated and the user must specify a price level."

---

name: Quote in a transaction currency with FX conversion and same-currency constraints
body:
- **name:** Quote in a transaction currency with FX conversion
- **user_flow:**
  1. Dynamics 365 Sales: create/edit the quote (or opportunity) → set the **Currency** lookup (a `transactioncurrency` record) and the **Price List**; the price list's currency must match.
  2. Dynamics 365 Sales: add products — the product lookup is filtered by the selected price list, and adding a product whose price list currency differs raises a pricing error.
  3. Dynamics 365 Sales: view totals — each money column is stored twice: transaction currency and `_Base` (organization base currency), with the read-only `ExchangeRate` column driving conversion.
  4. HubSpot: set the deal's **Currency** property; the quote's **Currency** label and formatting follow the deal. Account currencies are configured in Settings → **Manage currencies** and entered per-product and per-price-book.
  5. HubSpot: the quote editor's header module shows the currency; the *Totals* tab configures how discount is displayed (amount / percentage / both) in "the quote currency".
- **data_flow:** A `transactioncurrency` record (`ISOCurrencyCode`, `CurrencySymbol`, `CurrencyPrecision`, `ExchangeRate`) is chosen on the quote header (`transactioncurrencyid`) → line-item unit prices resolve from the `pricelevelproduct` row in that currency → totals (`totalamount`, `totallineitemamount`, `totaldiscountamount`, `totaltax`, `freightamount`) are computed in the transaction currency → the read-only `exchangerate` and `*_Base` columns (e.g. `totalamount_base`, `discountamount_base`) hold the converted base-currency view for reporting → on a wrong-currency combination, the platform refuses to price and sets `pricingerrorcode` (e.g. `34 Invalid Price Level Currency`, `38 Transaction currency is not set for the product price list item`).
- **data_sources:** Dataverse `transactioncurrency` table; `organization.basecurrencyid`; `pricelevel`, `pricelevelproduct`; quote/order/invoice `transactioncurrencyid` + `exchangerate` + `*_Base` columns. HubSpot deal/quote `Currency` property, account currency list, price book `Currencies` selection.
- **apis_hit:** Dynamics Web API: `GET /transactioncurrencies`, `POST /transactioncurrencies`, `PATCH /transactioncurrencies({transactioncurrencyid})`; the `RetrieveExchangeRate` message/event on the Currency table (`RetrieveExchangeRateRequest`, "Event: True"). `GET /transactioncurrencies(*transactioncurrencyid*)` for a single rate. HubSpot — `GET crm/properties/{version}/quotes` exposes `hs_currency`; `hs_currency` is a state-driven property populated on publish.
- **automations:** Currency/exchange-rate-driven recalculation on record open, create, update, and on product add/update/delete. HubSpot "quotes inherit the deal currency"; the quote's currency format is inherited from the deal record and "Changing the quote's locale settings won't update the currency."
- **features_tools:** Quote/order/invoice **Currency** and **Price List** fields; HubSpot quote **Header** module currency label; Totals tab **Total discount → Format** selector; **Manage currencies** settings page.
- **extensibility:** HubSpot — price books are single-currency ("Click the **Currencies** dropdown menu and select a currency"), so multi-currency is modelled as multiple price books; per-product price can be entered "in each of the currency fields". Dynamics — custom currency records (`CurrencyType: Custom`), plug-ins on pricing, and `exchangerate` is writable so a custom rate can be stamped.
- **sources:**
  - https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/developer/reference/entities/quote
  - https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/reference/entities/transactioncurrency
  - https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/sales/create-edit-quote-sales
  - https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/sales/price-calculation-opportunity-quote-order-invoice-records
  - https://knowledge.hubspot.com/products/use-price-books
  - https://knowledge.hubspot.com/quotes/create-and-send-quotes
  - https://developers.hubspot.com/docs/api-reference/latest/crm/objects/quotes/guide
- **evidence:** "Your base record and all its line items must use the same currency… You can't change the currency of the base record (in this case, an quote), unless you remove all the line items associated with the record." · "`ExchangeRate` — Shows the conversion rate of the record's currency. The exchange rate is used to convert all money fields in the record from the local currency to the system's default currency." · `PricingErrorCode` option 38: "Transaction currency is not set for the product price list item"; option 34: "Invalid Price Level Currency". · `TransactionCurrency` table description: "Currency in which a financial transaction is carried out." · HubSpot: "Quotes created from deals match the associated deal's *Currency* property."

---

name: Enforce configuration and discount guardrails with quote rules before publish
body:
- **name:** Enforce configuration and discount guardrails with quote rules
- **user_flow:**
  1. HubSpot: `Settings` → `Data Management` → **Objects** → **Select an object: Quotes** → **Rules** tab.
  2. Either click a **suggested prompt** in *Create a quote rule* (Breeze Assistant asks clarifying questions and drafts the rule), or click **Start from scratch** and type a rule definition in the quote-rules DSL.
  3. Under *Outcome* choose **Rule outcome type** = **Show warning** or **Block publish** → enter **Message to quote creator** → **Save rule**.
  4. Manage tab: open a rule name to edit, toggle the rule's **Status** off to disable, or delete it.
  5. A seller building a quote then sees the inline warning box in the line-items module, and publishing is blocked until the violation is fixed.
- **data_flow:** Line items, quote properties, and related records (deal, company, contacts, contract, quote template, current user) are read at rule-evaluation time → a SQL-like expression evaluates to true/false against the `WHERE`/quantifier/aggregate constructs → a true evaluation is a violation → violation either renders a warning banner in the quote editor with the configured message, or hard-stops the **Share/Publish** action, so the quote cannot reach the buyer.
- **data_sources:** HubSpot quote object, line items, product catalog (`hs_product_id`, `hs_sku`, `hs_product_type`), deal, company, contacts, `current_user` properties. Rule definitions are stored as text in the quote rules configuration.
- **apis_hit:** Quote rules DSL reference at `developers.hubspot.com/docs/api-reference/latest/crm/objects/quotes/quote-rules-syntax`; property validation resolves against `GET /crm/properties/...` (the "properties API"). Quote object endpoints for the evaluated record: `GET/PATCH /crm/objects/{version}/quotes/{quoteId}`.
- **automations:** Rules evaluate continuously while the quote is edited (warnings appear during build) and gate the publish step. Rules can be toggled on/off per rule; changes are staged in a sandbox environment for testing.
- **features_tools:** Settings → Objects → Quotes → **Rules** tab; rule editor with **Rule definition** and **Outcome**; Breeze Assistant prompt flow; **Block publish** outcome; **Manage** tab with per-rule **Status** switch; warning box in the quote line-items module.
- **extensibility:** The DSL is the extension surface — custom properties on any scope (`[quote.my_custom_property]`, `[line_item.x]`, `[deal.x]`, `[company.x]`, `[recipient_contact.x]`, `[current_user.x]`) are addressable; rules can be authored by prompt or hand-written; multi-branch workflows can be layered on top of the approval workflow.
- **sources:**
  - https://knowledge.hubspot.com/quotes/configure-quote-rules
  - https://developers.hubspot.com/docs/api-reference/latest/crm/objects/quotes/quote-rules-syntax
  - https://knowledge.hubspot.com/cpq/understand-hubspot-cpq
- **evidence:** "Use rules to display warnings when users build quotes or prevent them from publishing quotes until rule requirements are met." · "**Rule outcome type** … **Show warning:** display a warning when the rule requirements aren't met. **Block publish:** prevent users from publishing quotes when the rule requirements aren't met." · DSL examples: `SOLD_TOGETHER FROM line_item WHERE [hs_product_id] IN ("A","B","C")`, `INCOMPATIBLE FROM line_item WHERE [platform] IN ("legacy","modern")`, `SUM([quantity]) FROM line_item WHERE [hs_sku] = "ENT-LICENSE" > 5`, `[quote.hs_quote_amount] > 100000`, `MIN([hs_discount_percentage]) FROM line_item >= 5`. · Limitation: "quote-level discount properties are not available in the DSL." · "Arithmetic inside aggregate functions (e.g., `SUM([quantity] * [price])`) is not supported."

---

name: Route a discounted quote for standard approval
body:
- **name:** Route a discounted quote for standard approval
- **user_flow:**
  1. HubSpot (Super Admin): `Settings` → `Data Management` → **Objects** → **Quotes** → **Approvals** tab → toggle **Approvals** on → under **Standard approvals** click **Edit** next to *Quotes*.
  2. Under *And these conditions are met* click **+ Add filter** → **Filtering on** dropdown (quote, line item, deal, …) → **[Object] properties** → search and pick a property (e.g. quote amount, discount level, SKU) → configure the filter → **+ Add filter** for additional criteria.
  3. Under *Then do this* → **Approvers** dropdown → select the users who can approve. Under *Approver requirements* choose **All approvers required** or **At least one approver required**. Enter **With this approval note**. **Save** → toggle the **Quotes** switch on to activate.
  4. Seller: in the quote editor, hover **Request approval** → **View approval conditions** to see why approval is required → click **Request approval** → add **Notes to approver** → the quote moves to *Pending approval*.
  5. Approver: from the bell/email notification (**Go to quote**) or the quotes index page filtered to **Pending approval** → open the quote → **Approvals** icon in the right sidebar shows notes, approvers and activity → **Approve** (with an optional message) or **Request changes** (enter changes → **Reject**).
  6. On request-changes, the seller edits and re-submits; "if there's more than one approver, and one approver requests changes, every approver will need to approve the quote again when the quote is re-submitted."
- **data_flow:** Quote properties (amount, discount, line-item SKU/discount, related deal) are evaluated against configured property filters at publish → if a match exists, the quote's state moves `Draft → Pending approval`, approver identities are resolved from the configured user list, and an approval record + note + notification is created → approver decision writes `APPROVED` or `REJECTED` back to the quote and notifies the creator → only on approval can the quote be **Share**d (state `Shared`) and sent to the buyer.
- **data_sources:** HubSpot quote object, line items, deal; HubSpot user records (approvers, `Approve quotes` permission); quote approvals records; HubSpot notification/email delivery.
- **apis_hit:** Quote state is exposed on the object: `hs_status` (DRAFT / PENDING_APPROVAL / APPROVED / REJECTED / ACCEPTED …) via `GET`/`PATCH /crm/objects/{version}/quotes/{quoteId}`. `hs_locked` becomes `true` on publish and must be reset by moving `hs_status` back to `DRAFT`/`PENDING_APPROVAL`/`REJECTED` to edit. Quote reassignment/approval activity "may be available through APIs depending on how the event is configured and the permissions of the API request."
- **automations:** Approval enrolment and notification fire on the publish/share attempt; approval activity is written to the quote activity log automatically (`Quote approval requested`, `Quote approval rejected / requested changes`, `Quote approved`). Approval notifications can be delivered to third-party apps (Google Chat, Microsoft Teams, Slack) via Settings → Notifications → **Other apps**.
- **features_tools:** Settings → Objects → Quotes → **Approvals** tab; **+ Add filter** property filter builder; **Request approval** button; **Approvals** sidebar panel; quotes index page **Status: Pending approval** view; bell/email notifications; **Copy approval link** action on a published quote.
- **extensibility:** Filters can target any object (quote, line item, deal) and any standard or custom property; up to 10 approvers; approval note is templated per rule; you can turn **off** the *Create custom line items* permission to force standard pricing; legacy quotes offer a simplified "all quotes approved by one user" mode.
- **sources:**
  - https://knowledge.hubspot.com/quotes/set-up-quote-approvals
  - https://knowledge.hubspot.com/quotes/manage-quote-approvals
  - https://knowledge.hubspot.com/quotes/create-and-send-quotes
  - https://knowledge.hubspot.com/quotes/manage-quotes
  - https://developers.hubspot.com/docs/api-reference/latest/crm/objects/quotes/guide
- **evidence:** "Assign up to 10 approvers to review quotes that match your configured filters. Filters are based on properties and determine which quotes need approval." · "Require approval on quotes where a specific line item is above a certain discount amount." · "If a designated approver creates a quote, and they're the only approver, the quote won't require approval. If there are multiple approvers, they'll be removed from the approval process." · "Approvers can't approve their own quotes." · "A quote created via the API will automatically be set to `DRAFT`. Other states such as `PENDING_APPROVAL`,`APPROVED`, and `REJECTED` are primarily managed via the UI and approval workflows." · "`hs_locked` … Set to `true`. To modify any properties after you've published a quote, you must first update the `hs_status` of the quote back to `DRAFT`, `PENDING_APPROVAL`, or `REJECTED`."

---

name: Chain sequential multi-level approvals through a workflow
body:
- **name:** Chain sequential multi-level approvals through a workflow
- **user_flow:**
  1. HubSpot (Super Admin, Revenue Hub Enterprise): `Settings` → `Objects` → **Quotes** → **Approvals** tab → **Approvals** on → toggle **Advanced quote approvals** on → click **Edit** to open the approval workflow.
  2. Under the trigger, click **+** → left panel **Branch** → select **One property or action output** → choose the **Quote amount** property → **Next** → set the branch condition (e.g. greater than 5,000) → **Save**. Optionally enable **Re-enroll** in **Settings**.
  3. Under the criteria branch click **+** → **CRM** section → **Add quote approval step** → **Message to approver** (can embed quote properties via *Choose data variable*) → **Approvers** dropdown → **Priority** (for sequential) → **Save**.
  4. Click **+** again → **CRM** → **Start quote approval flow** → under *Approvers required* select **All approvers**, **Any approvers**, or **Sequential** → **Save**.
  5. Under the **None met** branch add **Go to action** → **Start quote approval flow** (so non-qualifying quotes skip approvals) → **Done** → **Review and turn on**.
  6. NetSuite equivalent: `Customization > Workflow > Workflows` → **New** (Record Type `Transaction`, Sub Type `Estimate`, Release Status `Testing`, **Execute As Admin**) → **Initiation** = Event-Based, Trigger Type `All`, Contexts `Web Store`, **On Create** → condition via **Visual Builder** (`Total` greater than or equal to `3000.00`) → **Save** → then define states **Estimate Creation**, **Pending Approval**, **Approved**, **Rejected** with **Set Field Value**, **Add Button** (Approve / Reject) and **Send Email** actions and conditional transitions.
- **data_flow:** Quote properties and related-record properties (quote amount, discount level, SKU, billing frequency, net terms, user attributes, related deal) are read by the workflow's branch engine → each qualifying branch pushes an *approval step* (approver list + priority) onto the quote → `Start quote approval flow` executes the chain, sequentially or in parallel, writing intermediate state and notifying the active approver → the last decision writes `APPROVED`/`REJECTED` and the quote becomes publishable. In NetSuite, the estimate row's custom **Approval Status** field is stepped `Pending Approval → Approved | Rejected` and an email is sent to the sales rep, with automatic approval when the rep has no supervisor.
- **data_sources:** HubSpot quote/line-item/deal/user properties; the HubSpot workflows engine; HubSpot notifications (bell/email/Teams/Slack/Google Chat). NetSuite: Estimate/transaction record, employee record (supervisor), custom body field for approval status, workflow manager state machine, email.
- **apis_hit:** HubSpot — workflow configuration is created/edited in the workflows tool ("The approval workflow is created using the workflows tool when advanced workflows are turned on"); quote `hs_status` via `PATCH /crm/objects/{version}/quotes/{quoteId}`. NetSuite — `Customization > Workflow > Workflows` with `GetDefaultPriceLevel`-style message registration is the analogous extension model; the documented example uses the **Condition Builder** and the **Workflow Manager** workspace, plus the `OrderQuoteApproval` workflow states.
- **automations:** Fully rule-driven, no user action needed to route. Limits documented: "You can add up to five sequences, and ten approvers per sequence"; "Sequential approvals require approval by every approver at each priority step"; "if a quote approval step hasn't been added above this action, quotes will be auto-approved." Re-enrollment can be toggled for quotes that need re-approval after edits. Notifications fire automatically on each step.
- **features_tools:** HubSpot workflow editor with **Branch**, **Add quote approval step**, **Start quote approval flow**, **Re-enroll** switch, priority ordering; Breeze Assistant can author the workflow ("use AI"); **Approvals** sidebar panel; NetSuite **Workflow Manager** (states, actions, transitions), **Add Button** actions for the web store, **Set Field Value**, **Send Email**.
- **extensibility:** HubSpot — you may branch on "one property or action output", use multiple branches for different approval types, and must use the single generated approval workflow ("You can't duplicate the workflow or create a new workflow to use for quote approvals"); users with *Edit permissions for workflows* can maintain it after a Super Admin turns advanced approvals on. NetSuite — new **States**/**Actions**/**Transitions** are added in the Workflow Manager; workflow ownership + `Execute As Admin` gives the workflow access to employee records; conditional transitions are driven by employee supervisor data.
- **sources:**
  - https://knowledge.hubspot.com/quotes/set-up-quote-approvals
  - https://knowledge.hubspot.com/quotes/manage-quote-approvals
  - https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/netsuite/ns-online-help/article_163853389082.html
  - https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/netsuite/ns-online-help/article_163878373827.html
  - https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/netsuite/ns-online-help/article_163853050104.html
- **evidence:** "Use **sequential approvals** ranked by priority. You can add up to five sequences, and ten approvers per sequence. For example, you could set a sales manager as first priority, a sales director as second priority, and a legal representative as third priority. The sales director won't need to approve the quote until the sales manager has completed their approval." · "Set Branch 1 to greater than 5,000. This would be the start of an advanced approval workflow for any quotes above $5,000." · "**Start quote approval flow:** if a quote approval step hasn't been added above this action, quotes will be auto-approved." · NetSuite: "This workflow starts when a customer submits a new order quote over a set limit, in this case $3000. The system checks if the sales rep on the estimate has a supervisor." · "Estimate Creation State … Transitions to … **Approved** if the estimate shows a default sales rep and that sales rep has no supervisor on their employee record." · "Add Button: Add an **Approve** button / Add Button: Add a **Reject** button."

---

name: Build a branded proposal from a template
body:
- **name:** Build a branded proposal from a template
- **user_flow:**
  1. HubSpot (Super Admin): `Settings` → **Branding** and/or `Settings` → `Objects` → **Quotes** → **Quote templates** tab → create a template. In the template editor configure each module: **header** (quote reference label, issue date, expiration date, currency label, PO number, logo), **parties** (seller, buyer, bill-to), **cover letter** / **executive summary**, **line items** (+ **Totals** tab), **terms**, **acceptance**.
  2. HubSpot: associate a **Brand** with the template (Enterprise); the brand appears top-right in the quote editor and drives logo/brand-kit colours; **Override brand kit** toggles and **Show company name when logo isn't set** control logo fallbacks. Logos can come from the quote branding settings, account branding, or the brand; images are chosen from the Files tool.
  3. HubSpot: hide/show sections with the view/hide icons; drag modules to reorder; in a rich-text section click **Advanced > Source code** to inject custom code.
  4. HubSpot: the template's cover letter / executive summary can be **generated by HubSpot's AI** "using data from line items, deal activities, meeting transcripts, notes, and emails."
  5. Dynamics 365 Sales: on any record, command bar → **Word Templates > Download Template** to get a Word file containing the entity's XML data → in Word enable the **Developer** tab → **XML Mapping Pane** → pick the schema starting `urn:microsoft-crm/document-template/` → right-click entity fields → **Insert Content Control > Plain Text** (Picture also allowed) → set repeating fields (**Repeating** on a table row) for 1:N data → save → **Word Templates > Upload Template**. Then on a quote: **Word Templates** → pick template to generate a populated Word document.
  6. PandaDoc: build a template in the editor containing a **pricing table**, **Content Placeholder (Smart Content)** blocks, fields, and approval-workflow configuration; content library items supply reusable terms/pricing/signature blocks.
- **data_flow:** Template definition (layout, module order, branding tokens, field bindings) + record data (deal, company, contacts, line items, quote fields) are merged at instantiation → either an HTML/JSON document model rendered by the HubSpot quote editor (and rasterised to PDF on publish) or a Word content-control/XML merge (Dynamics) → the resulting document is stored as the quote's presentation layer, with `hs_domain`/`hs_slug` deciding the public URL and the template id (`286` association) recorded on the quote.
- **data_sources:** HubSpot quote templates (`quote_templates`, `hs_type=cpq_template`), Brands, brand kit / account branding, Files tool, quote + deal + line item + contact + company records. Dynamics: document templates table, entity XML schema (`urn:microsoft-crm/document-template/`), `SharePointDocumentLocation`, Dynamics notes/attachments. PandaDoc templates, content library, pricing tables, folder hierarchy.
- **apis_hit:** HubSpot — `GET /crm/objects/{version}/quote_templates?properties=hs_type`; `POST /crm/objects/{version}/quote_templates/search` (filter `hs_type` CONTAINS_TOKEN `cpq_template`); quote↔template association type id `286` settable only at quote creation. PandaDoc — `POST /public/v1/documents` with `template_uuid`; `GET /public/v1/documents/{id}/details`; template management via `/public/v1/templates` (per `developers.pandadoc.com/llms.txt` index: create template, create from file upload, template details incl. `content_placeholders`, update tokens, share settings, folders).
- **automations:** AI module generation on template creation and on demand per module (Breeze icon). Template changes do **not** retro-apply: "Updating your logo and branding won't update existing published quotes, only currently drafted quotes and quotes created after updating."
- **features_tools:** HubSpot quote template builder, module editor, quote branding settings, Brands, **Customize quote style** action, **Advanced > Source code**, AI icon, desktop/mobile preview. Dynamics: Power Platform admin center → **Templates > Document templates**, Word Developer tab + XML Mapping Pane, security roles for **Document Template** vs **Personal Document Template**. PandaDoc template editor with Content Placeholder blocks, pricing table, `data_merge` column mapping.
- **extensibility:** HubSpot — **custom-coded modules** built with HubSpot CMS React/HubL (line-items table with sections, custom totals, billing schedule, ramps, conditional T&Cs by buyer country/product, custom parties section, custom nav menu, section-acknowledgment checkboxes); module source code editing; templates shareable; "API users can select templates that have custom modules included on them." Dynamics — full Word template control, `Repeating` content controls, entity relationships chosen at download, access controlled via security roles. PandaDoc — `content_placeholders` array replaces blocks with content library items at creation time (up to 10 items per placeholder), `data_merge: true` to use CRM-matching column names, `variables` in document titles.
- **sources:**
  - https://knowledge.hubspot.com/quotes/create-and-send-quotes
  - https://knowledge.hubspot.com/quotes/create-custom-modules-to-use-on-quote-templates
  - https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform/admin/using-word-templates-dynamics-365
  - https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/sales/create-quote-pdf
  - https://developers.hubspot.com/docs/api-reference/latest/crm/objects/quotes/guide
  - https://developers.pandadoc.com/docs/create-with-content-placeholders-from-template.md
  - https://developers.pandadoc.com/docs/working-with-pricing-tables.md
- **evidence:** "If your account uses Brands, the brand the quote is associated with is displayed in the upper right. The brand is set by the template used for the quote." · "The quote template's properties, content, and associations will be added to the quote as supplemental information, with properties set on the quote overriding the quote template's settings." · "It isn't possible to create or add custom coded modules to a quote using the API. API users can select templates that have custom modules included on them." · Dynamics: "Select the XML schema. It starts with `urn:microsoft-crm/document-template/`" and "you can only return up to 100 related records for each relationship." · PandaDoc: "Each content placeholder must be replaced with at least 1 content library item. You can add up to 10 content library items per content placeholder."

---

name: Publish and share the quote as a hosted link or email
body:
- **name:** Publish and share the quote as a hosted link or email
- **user_flow:**
  1. HubSpot: connect a domain (`Settings > Domains & URLs`); by default "quotes are hosted on the landing page primary domain connected to your account" and a separate subdomain (e.g. `billing.website.com`) can be used.
  2. HubSpot: in the quote editor top-right click **Share** (if no approval needed) → the quote moves to a *Shared* status "even if it hasn't been sent to the buyer."
  3. HubSpot: in the **Copy link, download PDF** tab click **Copy link** or **Download PDF** (live preview shown in the right panel).
  4. HubSpot: in the **Send quote email** tab — **To** auto-fills from the associated contact (changeable; a new email auto-creates a contact), **Cc** up to nine addresses, **From** defaults to the configured default from address, **Subject**, **Templates**, **Documents**, **Meetings** (scheduling page), body with formatting/personalisation tokens → **Send quote email**. The buyer receives the quote details, a link to view the quote in their browser, and a PDF attachment.
  5. HubSpot: from the quotes index page you can **Copy link**, **Download**, **Send by email**, or **Actions > Download published quotes** (a download link is emailed).
  6. Dynamics 365 Sales: open the quote → command bar **Export to PDF** → choose a Word template, set the **Save as** name → **Download**, or **Email** (the email form opens with fields prefilled and the PDF attached), or **Save to SharePoint** (default `SharePointDocumentLocation` = `<record_name>_<record_id>`) / **Save to Dynamics** (PDF stored as a note/attachment on the record). Mobile: **Create PDF** / **Email as PDF**.
- **data_flow:** Quote record + template + branding → rendered document → on publish the platform computes read-only properties `hs_quote_link` (public URL), `hs_domain`, `hs_slug`, `hs_locked=true`, `hs_pdf_download_link`, `hs_quote_number`, `hs_quote_amount`, `hs_language`, `hs_locale`, `hs_timezone` → a share/email event is created (tracking the recipient address) → the buyer receives an email carrying the link (and PDF if under 20 MB) and the quote becomes publicly viewable at the domain+slug URL. In Dynamics, the Word template merge produces a PDF that is then either downloaded, emailed, written to SharePoint's default document location, or attached as a note.
- **data_sources:** HubSpot quote object (`hs_quote_link`, `hs_domain`, `hs_slug`, `hs_pdf_download_link`, `hs_locked`), connected email/team email channel, HubSpot domains & URLs, Files tool. Dynamics `documenttemplate`, notes/attachments, `SharePointDocumentLocation` / SharePoint document library, Dynamics email.
- **apis_hit:** HubSpot — publish is state-driven on the quote object: `PATCH /crm/objects/{version}/quotes/{quoteId}`; `hs_quote_link` is "a read-only property and cannot be set through the API after publishing"; `hs_domain` and `hs_slug` are set by state. `GET crm/properties/{version}/quotes` returns the set. Dynamics — **Export to PDF** is a platform document-generation action (no public Web API endpoint documented on the pages read); SharePoint document location tables (`sharepointdocumentlocation`, `sharepointsite`) hold the output.
- **automations:** Publishing computes and freezes the totals: "The active quote state has the same price as the draft state. However, the overall amount is locked and can't be modified after it's published." Recurrence of automated reminders is configured in Settings → Objects → Quotes → **Reminders** tab (see workflow 14). Quote activity (`Quote published`, `Quote sent`) is logged automatically.
- **features_tools:** HubSpot **Share** button, **Copy link / download PDF** tab, **Send quote email** tab with live preview, **Send by email** action, **Actions** menu on the index page, domain/subdomain settings, default from address setting. Dynamics **Export to PDF** dialog with template selector and preview, **Email as PDF**, **Word Templates > Download/Upload Template**, SharePoint integration toggle + entity **Document Management** flag.
- **extensibility:** HubSpot — control the public surface via domain, `hs_slug`, password policy, identity verification, and locale/language; template source code and custom modules shape the document; branded PDFs are downloadable. Dynamics — new Word templates for any entity (`manage-word-templates`), custom file names, Save to SharePoint or Dynamics, accessible-PDF workflow (export to Word then Word's "Create PDF/XPS" with "Document structure tags for accessibility").
- **sources:**
  - https://knowledge.hubspot.com/quotes/create-and-send-quotes
  - https://knowledge.hubspot.com/quotes/set-up-quotes
  - https://knowledge.hubspot.com/quotes/manage-quotes
  - https://developers.hubspot.com/docs/api-reference/latest/crm/objects/quotes/guide
  - https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/sales/create-quote-pdf
  - https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/sales/create-edit-quote-sales
  - https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform/admin/using-word-templates-dynamics-365
- **evidence:** "By default, quotes are hosted on the landing page primary domain connected to your account." · "When you click Share, the quote moves to a *Shared* status, even if it hasn't been sent to the buyer." · "when you share a quote by email, HubSpot doesn't attach the generated quote PDF if it's larger than 20 MB." · "`hs_quote_link` — The quote's publicly accessible URL. This is a read-only property and cannot be set through the API after publishing." · "`hs_locked` … Set to `true`. To modify any properties after you've published a quote, you must first update the `hs_status` of the quote back to `DRAFT`, `PENDING_APPROVAL`, or `REJECTED`." · Dynamics: "the generated PDF file is always saved to the default location: `<record_name>_<record_id>`"; "You'll see optimum performance when the file size is less than 2 MB."

---

name: Collect acceptance by e-signature, countersignature, signer reassignment and identity verification
body:
- **name:** Collect acceptance by e-signature, countersignature and identity verification
- **user_flow:**
  1. HubSpot (Super Admin): `Settings` → **Objects** → **Quotes** → **E-signature** tab → toggle **Identity verification** on → select a **Verification from email address** (team email; individual work addresses can't be used as the default) → also set the **E-signature from email address** (else `success@hubspot.com`).
  2. HubSpot: monitor quota under *E-signature usage this month* on the E-signature tab; limits are pooled per account by subscription and seat count and reset on the 1st.
  3. Seller: quote editor → **acceptance** module → in the sidebar select **E-signature** → tick the buyer contacts under **Buyer contacts required to sign** (or **+ Add contact**), optionally enable **Quote signer(s) can reassign**, and select **Countersigners** from your organisation. (Alternative acceptance methods: **Print and sign**, or **Accept without signature** with **Request acceptance from** = *Do not specify* / a specific contact / added contacts.)
  4. Buyer: opens the shared link → enters the quote password if one is set → optionally **Reassign this quote signer** and submit new signer details → if identity verification is on, clicks **Verify email** in the *Acceptance* section → receives "Please verify your identity to sign your quote" (one-hour window) → clicks **Verify your identity and sign quote** → **Start signing** → **Get started** → **Click to sign** → **Draw/Type/Upload** → **Insert** → **Continue** → **I agree** → **Close**.
  5. Countersigner: receives an email; from `Revenue > Quotes` with status *Pending signature* → hover quote → **Preview** → **Actions > Countersign** → complete the signing steps. Countersigners who start first do not need to verify.
  6. After all signatures: the customer receives a copy of the signed document (link expires with the quote) plus a PDF. The seller can **Download** the signed PDF from the index page.
  7. PandaDoc equivalent: `POST /public/v1/documents/{id}/send` (optionally `silent: true`) → `POST /public/v1/documents/{id}/session` with `{recipient, lifetime}` → embed with the `pandadoc-signing` `Signing` library (`region: "com" | "eu"`) or share a link; identity verification is enabled per-workspace (passcode, SMS, KBA, ID check).
- **data_flow:** Quote acceptance configuration (`hs_acceptance_method`, signer contacts, countersigners) + buyer email → on send, a signing envelope is created (HubSpot's e-sign is powered by **Dropbox Sign**) → the buyer's identity is verified via an emailed one-time link (HubSpot/Dropbox Sign) before the signature widget unlocks → the drawn/typed/uploaded signature is bound to the quote document and a signature field record is written → the quote's signing status advances (`Pending signature` → `Viewed - pending signature` → `Pending countersignature` → `Accepted`) and `hs_clickwrap_accepted_by` / payment status update → activities (`Quote buyer signed`, `Quote countersigned`, `Quote reassigned`, `Signing attempt failed`) are appended to the quote activity log; if *Automatically create contracts from accepted quotes* is on, a contract (and, in Connected CPQ, an order) is created.
- **data_sources:** HubSpot quote object, contact records (signers/countersigners), user records (countersigners), Dropbox Sign e-signature service, verification email delivery (`success@hubspot.com` or a configured team address), quote activity log. PandaDoc: document, recipients, signature fields, `DocumentFields`, e-vault for the completed PDF.
- **apis_hit:** HubSpot — `POST /crm/objects/{version}/quotes` with `hs_acceptance_method` = `clickwrap` | `esignature` | `print_and_sign`; `hs_esign_num_signers_required`; `hs_clickwrap_accepted_by`; `hs_payment_status`; contact association type `702` (signer). PandaDoc — `POST /public/v1/documents/{document_id}/send`; `POST /public/v1/documents/{document_id}/session`; `GET /public/v1/documents/{id}/status`; `GET /public/v1/documents/{id}/details`; `GET /public/v1/documents/{id}/download` (and Download Protected Document for completed, production-key-only); `PUT /public/v1/documents/{id}/fields/assign` to assign/reassign fields; `PUT .../recipients` to change signer; `POST .../documents/{id}/session` with `lifetime` for embedded sessions.
- **automations:** Enabling e-signature on a **published** quote consumes quota immediately: "An e-signature will count toward the limit as soon as the e-signature option is turned on for a published quote. The quote doesn't need to be signed to apply to the signature limit." Multi-signature quotes count as one: "if a published quote with e-signatures enabled requires three signatures, this only counts as one usage toward your limit." Resending after expiry/recall costs another. Countersigners are emailed automatically when the buyer signs. Contract/order creation fires on acceptance. Signing-attempt failures are logged automatically.
- **features_tools:** HubSpot **acceptance** module, **E-signature** tab settings (identity verification, from-addresses, usage), signing widget (Draw/Type/Upload), **Reassign this quote signer**, **Verify email** step, **Actions > Countersign** on the index page, **Download** signed PDF, notification settings. PandaDoc Embedded Signing library, `document.viewed`/`document.completed` events, Identity Verification, signing order configuration.
- **extensibility:** HubSpot — countersigners are drawn from your own users; custom countersigner/buyer sets per quote; reassignment is per-quote configurable; `hs_acceptance_method` is scriptable via API; quote attachments can be marked **In signing** to be included in the envelope. PandaDoc — regions (`com`/`eu`), `silent` delivery for embedded/alt-channel signing, `forwarding_settings.forwarding_allowed` / `forwarding_with_reassigning_allowed`, `signing_order` per recipient, `role`/`roles` (signer, cc, approver), shared links vs embedded sessions.
- **sources:**
  - https://knowledge.hubspot.com/quotes/use-e-signatures-with-quotes
  - https://knowledge.hubspot.com/quotes/set-up-quotes
  - https://knowledge.hubspot.com/quotes/create-and-send-quotes
  - https://knowledge.hubspot.com/quotes/manage-quotes
  - https://knowledge.hubspot.com/contracts/set-up-contracts
  - https://developers.hubspot.com/docs/api-reference/latest/crm/objects/quotes/guide
  - https://developers.pandadoc.com/docs/embedded-signing.md
  - https://developers.pandadoc.com/docs/send-document.md
- **evidence:** "HubSpot's e-sign feature is powered by Dropbox Sign (formerly HelloSign)." · "Buyers have one hour to complete the signature process after clicking **Verify email**." · "if you download a signed quote, Dropbox Sign removes links from any hyperlinked text included in the *Cover letter*, *Executive summary*, or *Terms* sections from the PDF version." · "Attachments can be marked as *In signing* to be included in the signing envelope of an e-signature. If an attachment is marked *In signing*, e-signature must be used for the quote." · "Quote PDFs larger than 40 MB may not be successfully verified or signed." · PandaDoc: "It is your responsibility to verify the identity of any user who views a document within the signing session. Some use cases legally require Identity Verification to be enabled."

name: Accept a quote without a signature and take payment in the quote
body:
- **name:** Accept a quote without a signature and take payment in the quote
- **user_flow:**
  1. HubSpot (Super Admin): `Settings` → `Payment processing` → set the default payment methods and the buyer checkout experience; also `Settings` → `Objects` → **Quotes** for the default quote value (Quote amount vs Total contract value).
  2. Seller: quote editor → **terms**/billing area → **Enable billing** and online payments → choose **Billing**/payment options; note "if the quote offers online payments or the *Enable billing* switch is on, line item quantities must be whole numbers." Optionally set the effective date (**On agreement** / **Custom Date** / **Delayed start (days)** / **Delayed start (months)**).
  3. Seller: **acceptance** module → select **Accept without signature** → under **Request acceptance from** choose *Do not specify*, a specific contact, or added contacts. "This option can be used with or without online payments on the quote, and a contact doesn't need to be added to the quote." (Note: "online payments require an acceptance method of *E-signature* or *Accept without signature*. *Print and sign* isn't a valid acceptance method with online payments.")
  4. Seller: **Share** → **Send quote email**.
  5. Buyer: opens the link → clicks **Accept** (click-to-accept) → optionally **Set up payment** at the top of the quote; they can close and revisit the quote later to set up payment. HubSpot or Stripe payment processing charges the card, ACH, SEPA, BACS or PADS as configured.
  6. Automations: if *Automatically create contracts from accepted quotes* is on and you are in Connected CPQ, a contract plus an order are created and "The first invoice is also generated and sent to the buyer immediately after quote acceptance, regardless of its scheduled invoice date or due date." Otherwise, subscriptions/invoices are created for recurring/one-time line items.
- **data_flow:** Quote + line items (with billing start dates, frequencies, terms) → the publish step sets `hs_payment_status = PENDING`, `hs_billing_enabled = true`, `hs_payment_enabled = true`, `hs_payment_type = HUBSPOT | BYO_STRIPE`, `hs_allowed_payment_methods` → the buyer's accept action writes `hs_clickwrap_accepted_by` and flips `hs_status` to `ACCEPTED` → the payment processor creates a charge (min charge constraints apply: "the total amount due must be more than $0.50, or the equivalent minimum of the settlement currency") → an invoice (and, for recurring lines, a subscription, or a single contract in Connected CPQ) is created and emailed to the buyer/billing contact.
- **data_sources:** HubSpot quote + line items, contact/company (buyer + billing contact + billing company), HubSpot payments or a connected Stripe account, contract/subscription/invoice objects, tax rates (automated sales tax or per-line-item tax rates), `transactioncurrency`.
- **apis_hit:** HubSpot — quote properties via `POST/PATCH /crm/objects/{version}/quotes`: `hs_payment_enabled`, `hs_billing_enabled`, `hs_payment_type`, `hs_payment_status`, `hs_allowed_payment_methods` (`ACH`, `CREDIT_OR_DEBIT_CARD`, `SEPA`, `BACS`, `PADS`), `hs_collect_billing_address`, `hs_collect_shipping_address`, `hs_clickwrap_accepted_by`, `hs_collection_process` (`AUTO_PAYMENTS`), `hs_net_payment_terms`. Stripe minimums per `docs.stripe.com/currencies#minimum-and-maximum-charge-amounts` (linked from the KB page).
- **automations:** Publish-time payment provisioning; acceptance → contract/order/subscription/invoice creation; recurring invoicing on the contract's billing schedule ("Subsequent invoices are generated and sent according to the contract's billing schedule, 10 days before their invoice dates"); automated sales tax recalculated at quote creation using the billing/company address; quote auto-expiry and reminders (workflow 14).
- **features_tools:** HubSpot **terms**/billing module, **Enable billing** switch, **acceptance** module with **Accept without signature**, **Set up payment** button on the published quote, payment settings, automated sales tax toggle + **Tax category** column, **Totals** tab (simple subtotal vs subtotal with breakdown; how discount is shown; **Automated sales tax** off switch).
- **extensibility:** Billing frequency and billing start date are per line item (custom date, delayed by days, delayed by months) which supports ramped pricing; "Automated sales tax will be calculated when the quote is created"; sellers can allow the buyer to update billing address/tax IDs ("Buyers can add up to three tax IDs to the quote"); a "store the buyer's payment method for future charges" checkbox exists; HubSpot payments vs Stripe are swappable per account, and `hs_payment_type` is set automatically.
- **sources:**
  - https://knowledge.hubspot.com/quotes/create-and-send-quotes
  - https://knowledge.hubspot.com/quotes/set-up-quotes
  - https://knowledge.hubspot.com/contracts/set-up-contracts
  - https://developers.hubspot.com/docs/api-reference/latest/crm/objects/quotes/guide
  - https://knowledge.hubspot.com/quotes/manage-quotes
- **evidence:** "Accept without signature … This can be useful in situations where a formal signature isn't needed, such as for purchase orders (POs). This option can be used with or without online payments on the quote, and a contact doesn't need to be added to the quote." · "if the quote offers online payments or the **Enable billing** switch is on, line item quantities must be whole numbers." · "when using HubSpot payments or Stripe as your payment processing option, the total amount due must be more than $0.50, or the equivalent minimum of the settlement currency." · "The first invoice is also generated and sent to the buyer immediately after quote acceptance, regardless of its scheduled invoice date or due date." · "Quotes can't be voided or deleted after they have been accepted, e-signed, or marked as signed."

---

name: Secure quote access with buyer authentication
body:
- **name:** Secure quote access with buyer authentication
- **user_flow:**
  1. HubSpot (Super Admin): `Settings` → `Data Management` → **Objects** → **Quotes** → under *Buyer authentication* select **No authentication**, **Optional authentication**, or **Required authentication** → **Save**. (The setting applies to quotes created after saving.)
  2. Seller (if optional): quote editor → **Settings** (top right) → **Buyer authentication** → **Set a password** and enter a **password** → **Save**. "The password will be included in the quote email sent to the buyer when it is shared."
  3. Buyer: opens the quote link → is prompted for email address and the quote password before the quote renders/signs. Downloading the PDF from the quote email bypasses the password.
  4. HubSpot: separately enable **Identity verification** on the **E-signature** tab (workflow 10) so that even a link-holder must prove email ownership before signing.
  5. Also set a default **from address** and optionally **Allow sending from other email addresses**, and connect a domain so the public URL is on your own hostname.
- **data_flow:** Account-level auth policy (and per-quote password if set) is evaluated when the anonymous buyer hits the public quote URL at `hs_domain` + `hs_slug` → the document body is withheld until the supplied credentials validate → on validation the quote renders and acceptance can proceed. If identity verification is also on, a second challenge (emailed one-time verification link, 1-hour TTL) gates the signature step. The password is embedded in the share email; PDF download from that email is deliberately unprotected.
- **data_sources:** HubSpot quote settings (auth policy, default from address, domain), HubSpot domains & URLs, HubSpot team/individual email channels, Dropbox Sign verification emails (`success@hubspot.com` or configured team address).
- **apis_hit:** HubSpot — the policy lives in account settings, not a documented public API; the quote surface it protects is `hs_quote_link` / `hs_domain` / `hs_slug` on `/crm/objects/{version}/quotes/{quoteId}`. Verification and from-address settings are configured in the E-signature tab.
- **automations:** Auth is enforced on every anonymous access; the identity-verification link expires after one hour ("If you don't sign the quote within one hour of clicking *Verify email*, navigate back to the shared quote and click *Verify email* again to generate a new verification email"). Password and verification requirements apply to quotes created after the setting is saved.
- **features_tools:** **Buyer authentication** selector in quote settings; **Settings > Buyer authentication > Set a password** in the quote editor; **Verify email** step in the Acceptance section; domain/subdomain connection; **Default from address** + **Allow sending from other email addresses**; notification settings for verification-mail delivery troubleshooting.
- **extensibility:** Three policy modes (none / optional / required) let you pick the friction level; you can mix with identity verification; per-quote password is settable when the policy is *Optional*; you can force a separate subdomain for quoting; additional attachment files can be folded into the signing envelope.
- **sources:**
  - https://knowledge.hubspot.com/quotes/set-up-quotes
  - https://knowledge.hubspot.com/quotes/create-and-send-quotes
  - https://knowledge.hubspot.com/quotes/use-e-signatures-with-quotes
- **evidence:** "**Buyer authentication** … **No authentication:** buyers can view quotes without password authentication. **Optional authentication:** users creating a quote can choose whether to add password authentication to the quote. **Required authentication:** all quotes created must include password authentication." · "a quote link is public if the quote doesn't require email verification or isn't password-protected. Anyone with the link can view and sign the quote. If the buyer then shares the link, anyone they share it with may also be able to view and sign the quote." · "downloading the PDF of a quote from the quote email doesn't require a password." · "You have one hour to complete the signature process after clicking **Verify email**."

---

name: Track buyer engagement on a shared quote and drive follow-up
body:
- **name:** Track buyer engagement on a shared quote and drive follow-up
- **user_flow:**
  1. HubSpot (Super Admin): `Settings` → **Objects** → **Quotes** → under *Analyze quote activity level tracking threshold* enter the **high activity threshold**. Published quotes below it are classified *Low activity*.
  2. Any time: `Revenue > Quotes` → **Actions > Analyze your published quotes** → use the **time period** dropdown to filter by expiration date → in the *Your published quotes* bubble chart, quotes below the threshold render black and above it green; hover for name, expiration date and activity count; tick **Show older expired quotes**.
  3. Under **Pipeline overview** read the value of high-activity quotes, quotes at risk of expiring, and the quote acceptance rate; under **Recent quote activity** see name/last activity/amount/expiration; under **Recommended follow-ups** act on suggestions (e.g. no activity in a long time, expiring soon) by clicking **Send a follow up** which opens the **Send quote** dialog.
  4. On the index page, read the **Last Activity Date**, **Activity Count**, **Activity Count Since Last Communication** and **View Count** columns; filter by **Status**, **Last activity date**, **Owner**, **Signing status**, or **Advanced filters**.
  5. Open a single quote → **Preview** → *Quote activities* card in the right sidebar; or **Actions > Activity** for the full timeline. Deal board views show a colour-coded quote status chip on each deal card.
  6. Report further via `Actions > Go to quote reports` (revenue analytics suite) or custom single-object reports on the quote object; export all published quotes (`Export` / `Actions > Download published quotes`).
- **data_flow:** Anonymous and authenticated buyer interactions with the hosted quote (page views, PDF downloads, prints, clicks-to-sign) plus internal seller/approver actions are written as timestamped activity records against the quote → counters (`Last Activity Date`, `Activity Count`, `Activity Count Since Last Communication`, `View Count`) are maintained → the count is compared to the configured high-activity threshold to colour-code the quote and to drive the expiration/engagement bubble chart → the chart and Recommended follow-ups list surface at-risk quotes → the seller re-sends the quote email from the recommendation, generating a new `Quote sent` activity and (if previously expired/recalled) a new send.
- **data_sources:** HubSpot quote activity log (buyer + seller events), quote object analytics columns, quote index views/segments, HubSpot revenue analytics suite reports, custom reports, connected email channel (for "since last communication"), sales workspace / deal board views.
- **apis_hit:** HubSpot — activity/analytics columns on `/crm/objects/{version}/quotes` (read via `GET`); quote reassignment activity "may be available through APIs depending on how the event is configured and the permissions of the API request"; reports and exports run through `import-and-export`; **Download published quotes** delivers a link by email.
- **automations:** Activity events are written server-side without user action. The seller activity list includes `Quote published`, `Quote approval requested`, `Quote approval rejected / requested changes`, `Quote approved`, `Quote recalled`, `Quote countersigned`, `Quote reassigned`, `Signing attempt failed`, `Chat started` (buyer started a chat with the closing agent) and `Quote expired`. Buyer events include `Quote sent`, `Quote viewed`, `Quote downloaded`, `Quote printed`, `Quote buyer signed`, `Quote manually signed`, `Quote accepted`. Quote activity can be used as a **workflow** enrolment condition, and draft quotes "can be enrolled in workflows".
- **features_tools:** *Analyze your published quotes* dashboard (bubble chart, Pipeline overview, Recent quote activity, Recommended follow-ups), *Quote activities* card, full Activity timeline, index-page view tabs (expiring soon / pending acceptance / pending approval), Advanced filters with saved views, revenue analytics suite, board-view status chips.
- **extensibility:** The activity threshold is configurable; custom quote properties can be added (`Actions > Edit properties`) and used in filters; quotes can be associated to **custom objects** (Enterprise) to fold quotes into a bespoke data model; reports can be built on the quote object; the same activity stream feeds workflows and the Claude connector / Agent CLI (betas).
- **sources:**
  - https://knowledge.hubspot.com/quotes/manage-quotes
  - https://knowledge.hubspot.com/quotes/set-up-quotes
  - https://knowledge.hubspot.com/cpq/understand-hubspot-cpq
- **evidence:** "Published quotes with activity below this threshold are classified as *Low activity*." · "**Quote viewed:** the buyer has opened the quote using the quote link. If a buyer opens the PDF attached to the email, this doesn't count as a quote view." · "**Recommended follow-ups,** view recommended follow-ups for quotes based on activity on the quote, and expiration dates (e.g., quotes with no activity in a long time, or quotes that'll expire soon)." · "Quotes can have the following statuses, with a corresponding color indicator: … **Pending approval** … **Changes requested** … **Accepted**."

---

name: Expire a quote and auto-send buyer reminders
body:
- **name:** Expire a quote and auto-send buyer reminders
- **user_flow:**
  1. HubSpot (Super Admin): `Settings` → `Objects` → **Quotes** → set **Set a default expiration period** between 1 and 365 days → **Update**. "Any new quotes created after the setting is turned on will automatically use the configured expiration date."
  2. HubSpot: `Settings` → `Objects` → **Quotes** → **Reminders** tab → under *Reminder schedule* set the number of days and choose **Days after sending quote** or **Days before expiration date** → **+ Add reminder** / delete icon to manage several → set *Reminder send time* (in the account time zone) → **Preview reminder email** → toggle **Send automated reminders to quote recipients**.
  3. Seller: quote editor → **header** module → under *Expiration date* click the **date picker** to set a specific date, edit the **Label**, or toggle the **Expiration date** switch off.
  4. HubSpot: because a past *Effective date* is allowed, "the **Expiration date** will be treated as the buyer's sign-by deadline."
  5. PandaDoc equivalent: `PUT /public/v1/documents/{id}/settings` / auto-reminder settings configure automatic reminders after initial dispatch (email/SMS channel, initial delay, frequency); `POST /public/v1/documents/{id}/reminders` sends a manual reminder; `GET .../auto-reminder/status` reports per-recipient reminder status. PandaDoc documents also carry an `expiration_date` in state-change payloads.
- **data_flow:** Quote send/publish timestamp + configured expiry window → the quote carries an expiration date (`hs_expiration_date`; `expireson` in Dynamics) → a scheduled job evaluates sent/published quotes relative to that date and dispatches reminder emails at the configured offsets → if the buyer has not accepted/e-signed/marked-signed by the expiration date, the quote transitions to an Expired state (logged as `Quote expired`) and the buyer loses the ability to accept; expired quotes can still be downloaded, cloned, voided or archived, and resending counts as a new send (consuming e-signature quota again).
- **data_sources:** HubSpot quote object (`hs_expiration_date`, status), HubSpot transactional email, account time zone setting, quote activity log. Dynamics quote `expireson` / `effectiveto` / `effectivefrom` fields. PandaDoc document `expiration_date`, auto-reminder settings, per-recipient reminder status.
- **apis_hit:** HubSpot — `hs_expiration_date` is a required property on `POST /crm/objects/{version}/quotes`; reminder schedule is configured in settings (no documented public write API on the pages read). PandaDoc — `PUT /public/v1/documents/{id}/auto-reminder-settings` (update) and `GET /public/v1/documents/{id}/auto-reminder-settings` (retrieve), `GET /public/v1/documents/{id}/auto-reminder/status`, `POST /public/v1/documents/{id}/reminders` (manual), per the API index; `expiration_date` appears in the `document_state_changed` webhook payload.
- **automations:** Scheduled reminder dispatch (time-relative to send and to expiry, in the account time zone). Expiry check is a background job: "If a buyer hasn't accepted or signed a quote by the expiration date, it'll expire." Expiry semantics depend on acceptance method — e-signature/click-to-accept/print-and-sign each have their own "won't expire if" rule, and a quote accepted or signed but not countersigned or paid still does not expire.
- **features_tools:** Quote settings **Reminders** tab, **Preview reminder email**, expiration date picker + label, status filters for "expiring soon", *Analyze your published quotes* expiration filter, `Actions > Recall & edit` (possible before approval/acceptance/payment), **Void** (deactivates the quote link URL), **Archive** (unpublishes and hides from the default index view but blocks buyer access).
- **extensibility:** Multiple independent reminder rules; either offset (post-send or pre-expiry); per-timezone send time; a past effective date repurposes expiry as a sign-by deadline; reminder + expiration events are exposed as quote activities that can drive workflows.
- **sources:**
  - https://knowledge.hubspot.com/quotes/set-up-quotes
  - https://knowledge.hubspot.com/quotes/manage-quotes
  - https://knowledge.hubspot.com/quotes/create-and-send-quotes
  - https://developers.pandadoc.com/llms.txt
  - https://developers.pandadoc.com/reference/handledocumentstatechanged.md
- **evidence:** "Set a default expiration period for quotes… enter a default expiration time period between 1 and 365 days." · "If a quote is accepted or signed before the expiration date, but hasn't been countersigned or paid, the quote won't expire." · "**Archive:** … The quote is unpublished, hidden from the default index page view, and prevents buyers from accessing it." · "**Void:** … The quote link URL will be deactivated." · "Reminder schedule … **Days after sending quote** or **Days before expiration date**."

---

name: Auto-create a contract from an accepted quote
body:
- **name:** Auto-create a contract from an accepted quote
- **user_flow:**
  1. HubSpot (Super Admin): `Settings` → `Data Management` → **Objects** → **Contracts** → toggle **Create contracts from accepted quotes** on (or off).
  2. Optionally, in the same Contracts settings: **Renewals** tab → *Renewal is approaching alert* = `[x] days` / `Custom` / `Don't show an alert`; and on the **Setup** tab under *Deal creation* choose whether to auto-create deals for change/renewal quotes (with a chosen **Deal pipeline** and **Deal stage**).
  3. Buyer accepts the quote (e-signature, click-to-accept, or a HubSpot user marks it signed). A contract record is created automatically, inheriting line items, terms and other details from the quote.
  4. If enrolled in Connected CPQ, Billing and Payments: an **order** is also created and associated with the contract, and contracts own ongoing billing, invoice creation and payment collection.
  5. Review the contract: `Revenue > Contracts` → open the contract; the record shows inherited line items, terms, effective start date and totals; relate it to other records and export it.
  6. API/automation path: draft quotes can be enrolled in HubSpot **workflows**; the quote objects themselves are scriptable, so an integration can build the contract externally.
- **data_flow:** Accepted quote record (line items, term length, effective start date, currency, amounts) → platform copies the commercial content into a **contract** record, preserving line items and terms and setting the contract effective start date from the quote's *Effective* option (`ON_AGREEMENT` | `CUSTOM` | `DELAYED_BY_DAYS` | `DELAYED_BY_MONTHS`) → in Connected CPQ an **order** is created and linked → contract then drives invoice generation on its billing schedule and payment collection → the contract becomes the "centralized source of truth for committed revenue".
- **data_sources:** HubSpot quote object, line items, contract object, order object, invoice/subscription objects, deal, contact/company; billing processor (HubSpot payments / Stripe).
- **apis_hit:** HubSpot — quote state flips to `ACCEPTED` (set by the platform) and properties `hs_contract_effective_start_date`, `hs_contract_effective_start_date_type`, `hs_contract_effective_start_delayed_by_days`, `hs_contract_effective_start_delayed_by_months` are set on the quote; `hs_billing_enabled`/`hs_payment_enabled` drive invoice/subscription creation. Quote endpoints `GET/PATCH /crm/objects/{version}/quotes/{quoteId}`; contracts/orders via the generic CRM objects API.
- **automations:** Contract creation is fully automatic on acceptance, gated by a single setting with documented scenario matrix: setting on + Connected CPQ → contract **and** order; setting on, not in beta → contract only; setting off → no contract, but "Billing-enabled contracts and quotes create subscriptions, which are used to automatically invoice buyers and collect payments." Draft quotes use the *current* setting; already-published unaccepted quotes keep the billing flow in force at publish time; existing contracts keep the flow they were created under. Renewal alerts and renewal workflows are separately scheduled.
- **features_tools:** Contracts settings (**Create contracts from accepted quotes**, **Renewals** tab, **Setup > Deal creation**), contract record, renewal alert banner "before the renewal date", renewal workflow with a relative-date trigger (*Contract > Renewal date is less than [n] days from now*, with **Re-enroll**), Connected CPQ billing surface, `Revenue > Contracts` index.
- **extensibility:** Toggle semantics are documented per scenario; the "Direct Create, Edit, and Renew HubSpot Contracts" beta allows contracts without a quote; renewal alerts are days-based or custom; a renewal workflow can auto-create the renewal deal in a chosen pipeline/stage; quotes can be associated to custom objects; contracts can be exported and associated to other records.
- **sources:**
  - https://knowledge.hubspot.com/contracts/set-up-contracts
  - https://knowledge.hubspot.com/quotes/use-e-signatures-with-quotes
  - https://knowledge.hubspot.com/quotes/create-and-send-quotes
  - https://developers.hubspot.com/docs/api-reference/latest/crm/objects/quotes/guide
- **evidence:** "Contracts are the centralized source of truth for committed revenue in HubSpot." · "Set whether contracts are automatically created from accepted quotes. Contracts inherit line items, terms, and other details from the associated quote." · "Setting on. Enrolled in the Connected CPQ, Billing, and Payments beta. → Contracts are created when a quote is accepted. An order is also created, and associated with the contract." · "accepted legacy quotes don't create contracts." · "The state will automatically be updated to `ACCEPTED` when the buyer accepts the quote."

---

name: Create a renewal quote from a contract and auto-create the renewal deal
body:
- **name:** Create a renewal quote from a contract and auto-create the renewal deal
- **user_flow:**
  1. HubSpot: `Revenue > Contracts` → open the contract → in the left sidebar top-right **Actions** → **Create renewal quote** (or **Renew > Renew contract directly** if enrolled in the Direct Create/Edit/Renew beta).
  2. In the right panel: if *Automatically create new deals for renewal quotes* is on, pick the **Deal pipeline** and **Deal stage**; if off, **Associate with a deal** or **Create a new deal**.
  3. Choose a **quote template** (renewal/change templates), set the **Change effective date** via the date picker, optionally clear **Prorate charges and credits for the remaining billing period**, then click **Create quote**.
  4. You land in the quote editor with seller and buyer details auto-populated from the contract; adjust the *Summary* module (*Change effective date*: On agreement / Custom Date / Delayed start days / months), *Term length*, *Total discount* format, *Total contract value* → **Share**.
  5. Automated variant: `Automation > Workflows` → create/edit a deal-based workflow → set **enrollment triggers** → click **+** → **CRM** → **Create renewal quote from contract** → **Contract** dropdown (a recommended option or *Contracts: all associated*) → **Template** dropdown → **Deal selection method** = *New deal using default pipeline/stage* or *Existing deal* → **Save** → **Review and turn on**.
  6. After the buyer accepts: payment runs through the quote payment process, the **new contract is automatically associated with the previous contract**, and the renewal appears on the *Activities* and *History* tabs of both contracts.
- **data_flow:** Contract record (existing line items, term length, billing schedule, effective dates, currency) + renewal/change quote template → new quote record prefilled with contract seller/buyer data and the contract's commercial content, with a change effective date and optional proration → buyer accepts → a **new contract** is created and linked to the prior contract, forming a renewal chain, and a **deal** is created in the chosen pipeline/stage (or the workflow auto-creates one) to track the renewal opportunity.
- **data_sources:** HubSpot contract object, quote object, quote template (renewal/change), deal object, pipeline/stage configuration, billing processor, quote activity log.
- **apis_hit:** HubSpot — quote object create/update (`POST /crm/objects/{version}/quotes`) and association to the originating contract/deal; renewal quote template id attached as association type `286` at creation; contract renewal chain is surfaced on contract associations. The *Create renewal quote from contract* workflow action is a deal-based workflow action (workflows tool, not a documented REST endpoint on the pages read).
- **automations:** Deal creation can be fully automatic (setting or workflow action). The renewal **alert** appears on the contract "before the renewal date" using a configured day offset. Renewal workflows can trigger relative to *Contract > Renewal date* with an optional **Re-enroll** switch. On acceptance, contract-to-previous-contract association and payment/invoicing happen automatically. Note the workflow trigger semantics: "If a renewal hasn't been finalized, or a renewal quote isn't added to the contract, the renewal date will be the date the contract ends. If a renewal has been finalized or a renewal quote has been accepted by the customer, the renewal date will be the effective date of the renewal quote."
- **features_tools:** Contract **Actions** menu, renewal/change quote templates, quote editor *Summary* module, proration checkbox, contract **Renewals** settings with alert offsets, workflow **Create renewal quote from contract** action, deal pipeline/stage pickers, contract *Activities* and *History* tabs.
- **extensibility:** Choice of template per renewal; custom effective dates and delayed starts; proration toggle; deal auto-creation with configurable pipeline/stage (setting or workflow); direct contract renewal (beta) bypasses the quote; renewal workflow can target a single contract or *Contracts: all associated*; evergreen contracts (all line items set to *Automatically renew until canceled*) get special treatment.
- **sources:**
  - https://knowledge.hubspot.com/quotes/create-a-renewal-quote-on-a-contract
  - https://knowledge.hubspot.com/contracts/set-up-contracts
  - https://knowledge.hubspot.com/cpq/understand-hubspot-cpq
- **evidence:** "When a renewal quote is accepted, a new contract is created and automatically associated with the previous contract." · "Renewals can be created directly from a contract (BETA) or by using renewal quotes." · "**Create renewal quote from contract**" workflow action with **Contract** dropdown "(a recommended option or *Contracts: all associated*)". · "If a renewal has been finalized or a renewal quote has been accepted by the customer, the renewal date will be the effective date of the renewal quote." · "If all line items are set to *Automatically renew until canceled*, the term length is marked as *Evergreen*."
